pageDescription: Reads the enabled inbound Windows Firewall rules and flags missing programs, unsigned binaries and overly broad scope. Rules are disabled or deleted only after you confirm.
scanTruncatedNotice: The scan stopped early, so the list is incomplete. Scan again to check every rule.
toastApplyFailed: Could not change the firewall rules
emptyStateNoScanDesc: The scan reads only enabled inbound rules that allow traffic and changes nothing.
builtinTooltip: {{count}} Microsoft, system or packaged-app rules are hidden: they ship with Windows and should not be removed.
emptyStateNoMatchDesc: Change the filters or the search text.
summaryNonePartial: No rules to review among those read
summaryFacts: {{total}} enabled inbound rules · {{stale}} with a missing program · {{unsigned}} unsigned · {{broad}} with broad scope
receiptDisableReversible: can be re-enabled from Windows Firewall
receiptFailed_one: {{count}} rule not changed: the reason is listed below.
receiptFailed_other: {{count}} rules not changed: the reasons are listed below.
checkStaleDetail: Rules that point to an executable that no longer exists
checkUnsignedDetail: Executables outside the system folders without a valid signature
checkScopeDetail: Public profile with any port, or any remote address
confirmDisableDesc: The rules stay in Windows Firewall but stop allowing inbound traffic. You can re-enable them from Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security.
confirmDeleteDesc: The rules are removed from Windows Firewall. This is not reversible: to get them back they must be recreated by hand.
